derived_fields.chunk_count_by_width: read from plans[i].chunk_count in the source packet (1,1,1,1,1,1,1,2)
derived_fields.total_rows_by_width: sum of plans[i].chunk_rows; w8 is 256+32=288, and equals 36 x width here
derived_fields.packet_host_note: the packet's own host.cpu is "unknown" because platform.processor() returns empty on this host; this artifact's host block is derived from collect_artifact_provenance + /proc/cpuinfo, and the probe now stamps that itself

findings.finding: Every width up to 7 prefills as one chunk; width 8 (288 rows) splits into two slot-fair rounds because the resident slab is 256 rows.
findings.significance: the boundary is a buffer constant, not a scheduler policy; the planner is slot-fair, so a split round still visits all 8 lanes and never drops the tail

findings.finding: The slab is min(scratch.max_positions=256, linear chunk=256, full-attention chunk=256), so at this bench's default context all three terms are 256 and the cliff sits at 8x36 rows.
findings.significance: at a larger configured context (or longer prompts) the cliff moves; any claim like 'width 8 splits' is shape-scoped and must be re-derived per configuration, which is why the probe prints the constant instead of the tests hardcoding it

findings.cost: slab rows are BF16 activation scratch, so the trade is memory for a possibly-negative throughput gain; measure before changing the geometry
findings.finding: Despite splitting into two rounds, fresh admission rates rise through the boundary: C7 381.496 -> C8 409.029 tok/s (lane-weighted, 80 cells). The older grouped packet had C7 426.692 > C8 397.655.
findings.status: the extra parallel rows outweigh the extra round at this shape, so raising the slab to >=288 rows is a candidate improvement with an unknown sign, not a proven fix

findings.finding: I first recorded the hypothesis as disconfirmed because aggregate admission tok/s no longer dipped at C8. The constant settles it the other way: the split happens; what changed is that the split no longer costs more than it saves.
findings.significance: absence of a symptom is not absence of the mechanism - measure the mechanism

gates.arithmetic: no arithmetic change; probe is read-only
gates.note: this artifact records a geometry constant, not a performance claim

protocol.cross_check: the same planner run offline over 252/256/288 capacities reproduces the identical shape (tests/test_scripts_gguf_packed_prefill_slab_probe.py, CPU-only)
protocol.kind: geometry probe: loads weights, reads buffer geometry and plans chunk shapes; no timed arm, no flag, no state mutation
protocol.prompt_shape: 36 tokens per lane (canonical mtp-bench suite encoding length), valid ids cycled from the verifier prompt defaults
protocol.window: 23:00:32-23:01:39 local, after the d1 packet completed at 22:59:33 (no overlap)

question: At which wave size does packed AR prefill stop running as one chunk, and does that boundary explain the non-monotone grouped admission row (C7 426.692 > C8 397.655 tok/s)?
stop_rule: constant measured and cross-checked offline; the slab-size question now needs an A/B (slab 256 vs >=288 at C8), not more probing
